Harbor authority approves new container terminal

By Jane Doe, Port Correspondent

The regional harbor authority voted on Tuesday to approve a long-delayed container terminal, ending nearly six years of planning disputes and clearing the way for construction to begin early next year.

Officials said the terminal will add capacity for roughly 1.2 million standard containers annually, easing congestion that has repeatedly pushed shipping lines to divert cargo to neighbouring ports.

The distinctive turning point came when the board accepted a revised dredging plan that cuts the projected environmental footprint by almost a third compared with the original proposal.

Local business groups welcomed the decision, arguing that predictable berth availability would lower costs for exporters who have struggled with delays throughout the past three winters.

Environmental campaigners were more cautious, noting that monitoring commitments remain voluntary and that the authority has not yet published the independent assessment it promised last spring.

Construction is expected to take four years in two phases, with the first berths opening to traffic before the second phase of quay walls and automated cranes is complete.

The authority's chairman said financing was now secured through a mix of private bonds and a national infrastructure loan, and that tenders would be issued within ninety days.
